title: On Absorbing the heat of the day
subtitle: 生命科学 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 生命科学（科学与技术·生物与生命科学）
meta: 主题语境：生命科学（科学与技术·生物与生命科学）　|　核心词汇：absorb　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 absorb 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1989 the clerk ① absorbed the heat of the day in public, and every applicant in the office said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three months on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the clerk ② absorbs the heat of the day in silence without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ absorb the heat of the day at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ absorbed the heat of the day before — a line in the file for May 1983 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Absorbing the heat of the day in public, the clerk said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the stamp at the far counter, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ absorb every new word in the chapter in silence, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Absorb every new word in the chapter at once and never mention it again.

By 1996 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the file, and a new applicant from the next office ⑧ absorbs every new word in the chapter in public every month without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the counter, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ absorbed the heat of the day again when nobody else would.

⑩ To absorb the heat of the day, my mother said in 2001, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the office remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the office forgets, somebody absorbs the heat of the day in silence again and somebody must absorb the heat of the day in public all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 吸收（一般过去式 absorbed the heat of the day：1989 年书记员头一回这样做，当着众人面）
B. v. 吸收（一般现在 absorbs the heat of the day：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 吸收（不定式 to absorb the heat of the day：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 吸收（过去完成时 had absorbed the heat of the day：1983 年五月的卷宗上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 吸收（动名词 absorbing the heat of the day 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 弄懂（absorb every new word in the chapter：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去弄懂这一课的每个新词）
G. v. 弄懂（absorb every new word in the chapter：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 吸收（后段两处：新来的申请人照例 absorbs every new word in the chapter，而母亲又一次 absorbed the heat of the day）

answers.why: absorb 意为“吸收”，1989 年书记员当着众人面吸收白天的热气，那是办事处里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 absorbed。
absorb 意为“吸收”，自那以后书记员一言不发地把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 absorbs。
absorb 意为“吸收”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯吸收白天的热气”，此处为不定式 to absorb the heat of the day。
absorb 意为“吸收”，卷宗里 五月 那行字说明早在 1996 年之前就有人吸收过，故用过去完成时 had absorbed。
absorb 意为“吸收”，书记员说“吸收白天的热气这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 absorbing the heat of the day 作主语。
absorb 意为“弄懂”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去弄懂这一课的每个新词”，should ever 之后用原形 absorb every new word in the chapter。
absorb 意为“弄懂”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻弄懂这一课的每个新词（absorb every new word in the chapter at once），以后再也不要提起。
absorb 意为“吸收”，新来的申请人每个月份都照例弄懂这一课的每个新词，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 absorbs。
absorb 意为“吸收”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次当着众人面吸收白天的热气，用一般过去式 absorbed 叙述。
absorb 意为“吸收”，结尾那句是母亲 2001 年的话：要吸收白天的热气，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和办事处记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 absorb 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1989 the clerk absorbed the heat of the day in public, and nobody in the office forgot it.
Even now the clerk absorbs the heat of the day in silence whenever the office asks.
Absorbing the heat of the day in public, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever absorb every new word in the chapter in silence, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new applicant from the next office absorbs every new word in the chapter in public every month, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother absorbed the heat of the day again, and the office remembered that half.
